description: Ekibimiz başlangıç olarak liselerden oluşuyor. Her türden çalışma arkadaşına açığız ama eğlenmeyi sevenler daha önceliğimiz. Ekip olarak basit yazılım ve machine learning tecrübelerimiz var. Gelmek isteyen herkesi bekleriz.
summary: Mission Architect is a free, browser-based game for the “Space Mission Design Game” challenge. Players become a mission team and design a spacecraft for one of four NASA-style missions: an Earth wildfire watcher, a lunar ice hunter, a Mars climate orbiter, or a Europa ocean explorer. They choose the orbit, science instruments, power, antenna, propulsion and rocket. Five live gauges (money, mass, power, data and science) show every trade-off instantly, and each choice appears on a 3D model of the spacecraft. Players then launch on a rocket and fly the mission month by month. Team roles make the calls on surprise events. At the end, players get a score out of 1000, plain-language lessons, and a comparison with a real NASA mission. Under the hood, simplified real physics drives the game: the rocket equation, inverse-square signal loss, solar power and radiation. Real mission design is about balancing limits, and most people never see that. Our game lets anyone learn it by playing, with no prior knowledge or installation. It runs on phones, in English and Turkish, alone or as an online team.
details: Mission Architect is a free web game that teaches space mission design by letting players do it. Players choose one of four NASA-style missions, from Beginner to Expert: an Earth wildfire watcher, a lunar ice hunter, a Mars climate orbiter, or a Europa ocean explorer. They then design the spacecraft in a single workshop screen, picking the orbit, up to 14 science instruments, the power source, antenna, propulsion and rocket. Five live gauges (money, mass, power, data and science) show every trade-off instantly, and each choice appears at once on a 3D model of the spacecraft. The mission then launches in 3D on NASA rocket models and flies month by month around a NASA-textured planet. Surprise events such as collision warnings or instrument faults are decided by the responsible team role: Mission Manager, Spacecraft Engineer, Science Lead or Communications Lead. At the end, players get a score out of 1000, short plain-language lessons, and a comparison with the real NASA mission behind the scenario: Landsat 8, LRO, MAVEN or Europa Clipper. A simplified but proportional physics model drives every number: the rocket equation, the inverse-square law for sunlight and radio signals, eclipses, radiation and launch windows. The game shows why real spacecraft look the way they do, needs no installation or account, works on phones and offline, comes in English and Turkish, and can be played alone, as a team on one device, or in an online room, which makes it ready for classrooms. We built it with HTML, CSS and JavaScript on a standard laptop. Three.js draws the 3D scenes, Firebase Realtime Database runs the online rooms, and GitHub Pages hosts the site. NASA planet textures and 3D rocket models add realism. We used an AI coding assistant (Claude) and disclosed this openly. The creative core is that players build the spacecraft piece by piece, see it change in 3D, and then measure their design against a real NASA mission; a shared random seed gives every online teammate exactly the same flight without a game server. We focused on players of all ages: short jargon-free texts, keyboard support, readable fonts, strong contrast, reduced-motion and dark/light themes, and automatic quality scaling on slow devices. We tested the game balance over hundreds of simulated flights, added chat safety tools for online rooms, did not collect personal data, and credited all NASA sources.
